# Acknowledgements {.unnumbered}

My doctorate began with an email from Professor Louis Collins and ends with this thesis that would not exist without him.
For that first email, in which he believed in me and never stopped;
for each of the weekly meetings, where his guidance, support, and encouragement made me believe in myself;
and for all his advice and comments on presentations, posters, grant applications, and this thesis,
I am, and will be, immensely grateful.
His incomparable mentorship, characterized by his enthusiasm, dedication, and kindness, will forever guide me toward being
not only a great researcher, but a better person.

I would like to thank Professor Sylvia Villeneuve, who served on my
committee and whose guidance shaped the clinical direction of this
thesis. Her belief in me and my work extended beyond the committee
role. Even before moving on to the next stage of my career, she
has welcomed me into her lab and offered me the support and guidance
that convince me that the luck I have had with regard to mentorship will carry on.
I am also grateful to my committee members Professors Mallar Chakravarty and Danilo Bzdok,
whose insightful advice strengthened all four manuscripts that
comprise this thesis.

My thanks to Dr. Vladimir Fonov, whose technical expertise was
foundational to this work: his own quality control tool became
the basis for Qrater, and the convolutional neural network he
designed was adapted and trained for the hippocampal and ventricular
segmentation used throughout this thesis. I am equally grateful to
Dr. Dorothee Schoemaker, who proposed the hippocampal-to-ventricle
ratio, the measure on which this entire thesis rests. To my
labmates, past and present, who helped test and refine Qrater
through literally tens of thousands of images; to my co-authors, who reviewed and
strengthened each manuscript; and to the technical team behind the
Brain Imaging Centre, this work would not have been possible
without you.

This investigation was supported by the Canadian Institutes of
Health Research, the International Progressive MS Alliance, and a
generous donation from the Famille Louise & André Charron.

To Professors Mahsa Dadar and Yashar Zeighami and their laboratory, thank you for your professional camaraderie.
I appreciate each and every one of your team photos that I have crashed.

My heartfelt appreciation to Aliza Brzesinski, my favourite colleague; Alda Profka, my first family in Canada;
and Sonny Vazquez, who taught me that friendship knows no distance nor borders; to all of you, thank you.

Last, but definitely not least, to my parents and my siblings, whose love and affection kept me warm during
the coldest winters: Gracias y los amo.
